verdict: Ads went dark two days; cost per lead spiked as a result.
narrative: This period you received 121 leads at a 28-day blended cost of $6.25 per lead — but the last seven days tell a sharper story: leads fell 26% while spend climbed 55%, driving cost per lead up 110% week-over-week. The direct cause is a confirmed two-day delivery outage on October 6–7, where Meta ran zero spend and produced zero leads; average daily spend in the last three days was $11.65 versus $43.50 in the three days prior. Separately, nearly all of your budget this period ran through a single campaign, leaving no backup delivery when that campaign paused. Meta has been reactivated and campaign structure is being broadened this week so that a single pause cannot collapse overall delivery again.

highlights.phrase: leads received in the last 28 days, all from Meta
cost per lead this period, up from roughly $3.00 the prior week due to the outage
days Meta ran dark (Oct 6–7), the confirmed source of the cost spike

watch_item.issue: A single campaign absorbed 87% of this period's budget, meaning any delivery disruption hits your lead volume with no cushion.
watch_item.fix: Campaign structure is being diversified this week to spread delivery across multiple campaigns, reducing concentration risk.
